title: App update check with the update offer over IPC and the auto-update setting
story: Grillo now looks for a newer version on its GitHub Releases page when it starts and every hour after that, and sends the offer, the download progress and ready-to-install to the setup screen, which draws the update card in its own story. There is no pop-up window. With the App updates switch on, the new version downloads quietly and installs when Grillo closes; an unsigned Mac build only offers a manual install, and npm run dev never checks at all.

checks.criterion: An unsigned build or a dev run never errors loudly; the check logs and returns
checks.steps: In a fresh checkout run npm ci, set GRILLO_DEV_PORT, run npm run dev, and watch the terminal for 20 seconds.
checks.expected: The line "Update check skipped: this is a development run, not an installed app", and no error or stack trace.

checks.criterion: The setup screen can read the update state and change the auto-update setting
checks.steps: With npm run dev open, open DevTools and run await window.grillo.invoke('updates:get-state'). Then run await window.grillo.invoke('updates:set-auto-update', true), close Grillo, and open the app data folder's settings.json.
checks.expected: The state is { currentVersion: '0.1.0', phase: 'none', version: null, percent: null, autoUpdate: false, manualInstall: false } on Windows (manualInstall: true on a Mac). The second call returns autoUpdate: true, and settings.json holds "autoUpdate": true.
